data.content_ref: inline:The isolated artifact contradicts the foundational assumption shared across the neighbourhood — that decorrelation is achievable through a deterministic oracle (SRC_001, SRC_005) — by arguing that any single engine mediating access to even a deterministic oracle introduces an epistemic bottleneck: the engine must interpret, format, and report the oracle's output through its generative prior, meaning the verifier's verdict is never causally decorrelated from the engine's claim-generation process regardless of the oracle's determinism. Weight freezing (SCR_001) does not solve this because the generative prior still mediates the query and the response interpretation. This contradicts SRC_001's claim that a self-executed test yields an external observable distinct from the claim text, because the distinctness of the observable does not guarantee the distinctness of its interpretation. The covering principle fails at the interpretation layer even when it holds at the execution layer. This is REFUTED IF an ablation test (SCR_002) demonstrates that the checker's verdict systematically flips when the oracle's reported output is perturbed — because that would prove the verdict is causally sensitive to the oracle result and not merely to the engine's interpretation of it.
